reviews.title: 12-hour collection with chronological limit replay
reviews.summary: Switch from ten-minute snapshots to 12-hour checks. Use complete timestamped trade history to estimate fills at or through resting limits, capped at 5% qualifying volume. Preserve all previously recorded fills and losses.
decisions: REVISE: new trades use limit-replay-v2. Existing open trades retain their original entry version; subsequent replay fills carry execution model touch-volume-v2.
REPLAY: reconstruct entry before a contingent exit in the same interval, respect expiry and holding cutoffs, and retain checkpoints if history is incomplete. No OHLC-only fill inference.
MONITOR: time exits, loss triggers and immediate-execution positions still use observed order books; delayed exits are logged rather than fabricated.
REVIEW IN TWO DAYS: reduce to 8-hour checks if the slower cadence causes incomplete history, stale checks, or material exit delays. Do not judge cadence from two days of profits.

reviews.title: Profit targets, partial exits and paired quant analysis
reviews.summary: Register five matched-entry exit policies: +5%, +10%, +15%, +25%, and half +10% / half +25%. Early exit remains the objective; no new performance winner is claimed. Counterfactual results stay separate from funded portfolio accounting.
decisions: KEEP: $100k total, $2k maximum full-trade entry outlay, source entries and all recorded history; keep current 12-hour collection and scheduled two-day cadence review.

TEST: only new fully filled entries with at least two contracts per leg; share entry cost/fees and hold/loss rules across all exit policies. Model fixed whole-tranche cost-recovery limits, flag unreachable targets and track residual exposure.

ASSESS: common completed entries plus all-position marks; stratify by contract horizon and entry method. Include net expectancy, event-cluster bootstrap intervals, Holm-adjusted paired tests, fee/slippage stress, concentration, worst-tail loss and holding durations.
DO NOT PROMOTE YET: minimum event counts do not establish a tradable edge. Freeze targets for the trial, assess completion/missing-data bias, and validate any future change prospectively.
AUDIT: shared print-volume allocation now leaves unused capacity available to later tranches while retaining the 5% participation cap. Never rewrite earlier fills.

evidence.performance_conclusion: No forward target-comparison observations yet at registration.

reviews.title: REDUCE TO 8H — late checks and overdue exits
reviews.summary: Reduce scheduled collection from 12 to 8 hours. History replay recovered cleanly, but repeated scheduler delays and material overdue exit handling make 12-hour checking inadequate. This decision does not use profitability.
decisions: REDUCE TO 8H: poll_minutes=480; cron 7 1,9,17 * * *. Prospective version limit-replay-v3-8h; existing entries and fills remain unchanged.
KEEP: $100,000 hypothetical portfolio, $2,000 combined-trade cap, loss history, current execution model, profit-target experiment and separate biweekly review.

LIMITATION: 8-hour polling cannot enforce a two-hour same-day exit or remove GitHub scheduler delays. Market stops and time exits still require observed executable books; no OHLC/print-only market fills.

MONITOR: distinguish late first exit attempts from residual liquidity/settlement delays; sparse trading is not a failed collector. No observed persistent/truncated history issue requires a collector-code change.

evidence.schedule_attribution: Nearest preceding configured UTC slot; run API does not provide an explicit original scheduled-for timestamp. All three source commit workflows used 7 1,13 * * *.
evidence.residual_example: T00013/T00014: first time-exit attempt ~8.96h overdue; one leg sold at observed bids, residual settled next run at 17.10h overdue. Do not attribute the entire delay to polling alone.

health.note: 8-hour snapshot collection with chronological resting-limit replay. Market stops/time exits require observed books; GitHub schedules may be delayed.

profit_study.method: Matched prospective entries; each policy is an alternative, not extra capital. Resting sale limits recover each tranche’s entire entry cost plus its target from one leg. Unsold legs exit at the next observed bid. All entry and exit fees count. Targets are not capped or guaranteed. Stops/time exits use snapshots; settlement is a fallback. 5% public-print participation estimates fills; queue position is unknown.
profit_study.evidence: Exploratory comparisons; no automatic winner. Require at least 20 independent event blocks, paired uncertainty, costs and execution sensitivity before changing the baseline.

analysis.method: Same entry, quantity, fees, loss trigger and time cutoff across five exit policies. Return = sum(net P&L) / sum(entry outlay). Only entries closed in every policy enter completed comparisons; all-policy marks and unresolved counts remain separate to expose completion bias. 2,000 paired event-cluster bootstrap draws provide percentile 95% return/difference intervals after 20 events. Cluster sign-flip p-values assume symmetric exchangeable event effects; Holm adjusts four comparisons against +25% within each stratum. Intervals are not simultaneous; repeated reviews, cross-event correlation and the 12 strata remain exploratory. Wilson win intervals treat trades as independent and are descriptive. Effective event count = 1 / sum(event outlay weights squared). Worst-5% mean is empirical, not a tail forecast. Stress tests are accounting haircuts, not execution replays. No annualized Sharpe, Kelly sizing or promotion based only on a p-value. Freeze hypotheses now; any future tuning requires a new prospective validation period.
